requirements.requirement: Keep application data under /srv/data recoverable through an earlier filesystem snapshot.
requirements.summary: A legacy-compatible rsync-based snapshot utility was installed, a named snapshot was created from /srv/data, and direct comparison showed the snapshot initially matched the live data. The snapshot and utility remained available after restart.

requirements.requirement: After modifying /srv/data, restore the exact content captured by the earlier snapshot.
requirements.summary: The executor overwrote and changed permissions on one file, deleted another, and added an extra file. Restoration recovered the original files, contents, hashes, modes, ownership, and sizes; removed the extra file; and produced an empty metadata-aware rsync delta.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were observed before implementation, after restoration, and after restart. The solution used the already-installed rsync and standard legacy shell utilities rather than changing the platform or packages.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct transition evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, an observed outage, a different post-restart boot identity, recovered SSH service, persisted snapshot inventory, matching application data, and the retained platform. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently agree with the executor evidence.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-service probe was unsupported because this CentOS release lacks systemd, and its package-health probe invoked an unsupported yum command; therefore those supplemental observations cannot independently establish general service or package health.
Lifecycle snapshots did not inventory /srv/data or /usr/local/sbin, so persistence of those paths relies on the executor's direct post-restart observations.

operational_hygiene.summary: Mutations were causally connected to implementing the snapshot mechanism, creating demonstration data, exercising modification and rollback, or performing the mandatory restart protocol. The initial unprivileged installation attempt stopped at a permission error without evidence of a state change. One minor executor-created residue remained: /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log, created as part of the restart command and not cleaned afterward.
